activities.anchor: The shop concentrates several classes of hazard into one room
activities.caption: file the hazard — which class owns it?
activities.name: sssHazardBuckets

config.prompt: One room, several hazard classes — file each:

items.label: fuel vapour ignites from sparks you cannot see
brake cleaner never sprayed near a running engine or catalytic converter
rotating belts and fans take fingers
hot coolant scalds at opening pressure — cap released slowly, cold engine first
compressed air above roughly 30 psi can drive debris through skin
orange cables carry 400–800 volts demanding certified EV training

config.why: Every class of hazard has an engineered defence, and PPE is the last line, not the first.

activities.anchor: rotating belts and fans take fingers
activities.caption: call the magnitude — the air-injection threshold
activities.name: sssAirEstimate

config.prompt: Tyre pressures run around 35 psi, and shop air lines run far higher. Above roughly what pressure can compressed air drive debris through skin?
config.why: About 30 psi — the reason air lines are treated as injection hazards, not splashes: debris-driven air is a medical emergency.
config.context: The same respect applies to hydraulics: a vehicle raised off the ground is a couple of tonnes of stored gravitational energy.

activities.anchor: Personal protective equipment is the last line
activities.caption: pair each hazard with its PPE
activities.name: sssPpeMatch

config.prompt: PPE is matched to the task — pair the hazard with its defence:

pairs.right: safety glasses from the first minute
steel-toe boots — it weighs what a bowling ball weighs
housekeeping — a shop's floor condition predicts its injury record

config.why: Two habits summarise the whole safety module: protect yourself first, and never let time pressure talk you out of a step.

activities.caption: find the faulty line — tool discipline
activities.name: sssToolSpot

config.prompt: This tool-cart briefing contains one faulty line — click it:
lines: Hand tools are organised by drive size and system.
Torque wrenches are for anything with a specification.
An uncalibrated torque wrench is a random-number generator pointed at a wheel bearing.
Any size wrench works if you push hard enough — a rounded-off bolt just needs muscle.
Specialty tools the manufacturer requires — like for timing chains — get used, not improvised.
config.correction: Use the right size: a rounded-off bolt is a 20-minute problem created in 2 seconds — and calibrate the torque wrench.
config.why: The two habits that separate professionals: the right size, always, and a calibrated torque wrench for anything with a spec.

activities.anchor: Two-post lifts add their own liturgy
activities.caption: rebuild the two-post lift procedure, step by step
activities.name: sssLiftOrder

config.prompt: The liturgy that keeps tonnes off people — put it in order:
items: know the vehicle's weight against the lift's rated capacity
position the arms at the factory-marked lift points
raise to just off the floor
push the vehicle to confirm balance
raise fully and engage the mechanical safety locks
config.why: A lift rated for 4,000 kg does not become 4,500 kg because you hope — and even a correctly placed lift can tip an unbalanced load. The checks cost ninety seconds; the failure mode is measured in tonnes.

activities.anchor: I'm only going under for a second
activities.caption: bet first — 'just a second' under the jack
activities.name: sssSecondPredict

config.q: A colleague says 'I'm only going under for a second' — car still on the jack. What does the trade's record say happens?
choices: almost nothing — seconds are safe while the seal is new
the vehicles that fall are overwhelmingly the ones someone believed would be fine for a moment
falls only happen with old, worn-out jacks
config.why: Every safety rule in the lifting section is a memorial to exactly that sentence — hydraulics hold weight, they do not hold responsibility, and a seal can fail silently.

activities.anchor: Battery work has its own liturgy
activities.caption: run the disconnect — battery terminal sequence
activities.name: sssBatteryBranch

config.root: You need to disconnect a 12-volt battery to service the charging system. Hydrogen vents during charging; acid is in the cells.

choices.label: Positive first, then negative
choices.feedback: Backwards — and the reason is in your hand.

choices.label: No disconnect — just be careful around the terminals

backwards.text: Disconnecting positive first leaves your wrench one slip away from shorting across the terminals — the arc happens with your hand on the tool.

correct.text: Negative first, reconnect last: no sparks near venting hydrogen, gloves and eye protection for the acid, and the wrench can never complete the circuit across the terminals.

careful.text: Disconnecting order exists precisely because a wrench across the terminals is an arc with your hand on it — gloves and caution do not replace the procedure.

config.why: Fluids and batteries each carry a handling discipline: used oil is collected, coolant is wiped immediately, brake fluid stays sealed, refrigerants belong to certified technicians.

activities.anchor: the three-part record the industry expects
activities.caption: fill the blanks — the work order's three parts
activities.name: sssRecordCloze

config.text: Outbound, the technician writes the three-part record: the %%0%% (as verified), the %%1%% (the diagnosis, with the tests that proved it), and the %%2%% (the repair performed, the parts replaced, the verification run).
config.hint: What the customer brought, why it happened, and what you did about it — the diagnostic method's paperwork twin.
